nodes.summary: Let $x$, $a$, $b$ be positive integers with $a + b \le 10$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$ if and only if $x = 1$ and $a = 1$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products with $a + b \le 10$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{1+2b}{b}$ if and only if $a = 1$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products with $x = 1$

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $b$ be positive integers and let $a$ be a nonnegative integer. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$ if and only if $x = 1$ and $a = 1$.
nodes.title: Allen's theorem on central binomial products

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $b$ be positive integers and let $a$ be a nonnegative integer with $a \le x$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \le \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$, and equality holds if and only if $x = 1$ and $a = 1$.
nodes.title: Allen's inequality for central binomial products

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $4 < 2a \le a + b$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{a+2b-2}{b}$, so the equation $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$ has no solution with $x = a - 2$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products in the case $x = a - 2$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $4 < 2a \le a + b$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{a+2b-3}{b}$, so the equation $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$ has no solution with $x = a - 3$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products in the case $x = a - 3$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $4 < 2a \le a + b$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{a+2b-1}{b}$, so the equation $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} = \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$ has no solution with $x = a - 1$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products in the case $x = a - 1$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, let $x \ge 2$ be an integer, and put $k = a + b$. If $k \ge 75$, $a \le \tfrac{9}{10}k$ and $b \le \tfrac{4}{5}k$, then $\binom{2k}{k} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products in the balanced range

nodes.summary: Let $x$, $a$, $b$ be natural numbers with $x \ge 1$ and $3 \le b \le a$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products with $a \ge b \ge 3$

nodes.summary: Let $x$, $a$, $b$ be natural numbers with $x \ge 2$ and $1 \le b \le a$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products with $x \ge 2$ and $a \ge b$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $x$ with $b \ge 1$, $x \ge 2$, $a + b \ge 150$ and $a \ge \frac{171}{121} x$, we have $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: No large solutions of the central binomial product equation with a dominant central factor

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $x$ with $a \ge 1$, $b \ge 1$, $x \ge 2$ and $a + b \ge 150$, we have $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: No large solutions of the central binomial product equation with shift at least two

nodes.summary: Let $x$, $a$, $b$ be natural numbers with $a \ge 1$, $b \ge 1$, $x \ge 2$ and $x < a + b < 150$. Then $\binom{2(a+b)}{a+b} \ne \binom{2a}{a}\binom{x+2b}{b}$.
nodes.title: Central binomial products with $x \ge 2$ and $a + b < 150$

nodes.title: Stănică's bounds for the binomial coefficient $\binom{mn}{rn}$

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $m > 3$, $n > 4m$ and $n + m \ge 150$. Then the product $n(n+1)\cdots(n+m-1)$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > 4.42\,m$.
nodes.title: A prime factor above $4.42m$ in a product of consecutive integers

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $2 < m < n$ and $n + m \ge 150$. Then the product $n(n+1)\cdots(n+m-1)$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > 9m/5$.
nodes.title: A prime factor above $9m/5$ in a product of consecutive integers

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $0 < m < n$. The product $n(n+1)\cdots(n+m-1)$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > 3m/2$ if and only if $(n, m)$ is none of the pairs $(3, 2)$, $(8, 2)$ and $(6, 5)$ (the products $3 \cdot 4$, $8 \cdot 9$ and $6 \cdot 7 \cdot 8 \cdot 9 \cdot 10$).
nodes.title: Hanson's theorem on a prime factor above $3m/2$ in consecutive integers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
